name: Continuous Shot
visualIdentity: Normalized from an explicit request for one continuous shot. One readable camera path through connected space preserves subjects, lighting, and occlusion; internal action, scale changes, and transformations shape the sequence. Avoid resets, wall intersections, and hidden cuts.
suitableUses: Suitable for videos or interactive HTML that benefit from a sustained spatial journey, such as company tours, process walkthroughs, product passages, or immersive narratives. These use cases are inferred from the supplied combinations and compatibility notes.
limitations: Dense text is hard to read during travel; provide frontal reading holds. Avoid when stable orientation or reduced motion is needed. Do not claim a flat image move is a 3D dolly. Orbit needs full geometry or sufficient turntable views; omit unsupported patterns.
palette: No intrinsic palette is specified. Preserve task, brand, reference, and existing semantic colors and material families. Optional example tokens are background #F2EBDD, foreground #343E43, accent #8D957D; they are not canonical. Keep discrete colors; gradients are disabled. Accent with foreground yields 3.511 contrast, unsuitable for normal text; verify actual compositing.
motionAndInteraction: Build a continuous scene and camera curve; derive pose from shared composition time and cache or deterministically replay simulation for direct and backward seeks. Use deliberate acceleration and pauses, preserve readable endpoints, and assign one owner per animated property. For HTML, finite scroll progress may drive reversible states with keyboard and reduced-motion alternatives; video must not depend on live input. Candidate vortex, orbit, story-step, or dolly patterns require their stated geometry and narrative rationale.
audio: No fixed soundtrack is specified. Suggest music, narration, vocals, effects, ambience, or silence for the subject and audience; honor supplied choices. Synchronize and mix through the render pipeline, then check intelligibility, balance, clipping, and picture sync.
assetRequirements: Inspect source assets, exact copy, and formats first. A dolly needs real depth or a disclosed 2.5D approximation; orbit needs a complete subject or sufficient captured views. Load local fonts and assets, seed randomness, and cache stateful simulations. Do not invent available audio assets.
combinations: Style 079 diorama supports a bounded, consistent-scale world for tours; keep one camera spline and avoid wall crossings. Style 093 spatial signage can carry narrative if text faces the camera for reading holds. Three.js is the single renderer in these suggestions; preserve accessibility with DOM text. These are suggested combinations, not requirements.
productionApproach: Select renderer and motion method by style and fidelity: Three.js for scene, camera, geometry, materials, and lighting; GSAP for authored seekable motion. HyperFrames owns assembly, timing, synchronization, validation, and export. Use Remotion only if HyperFrames is unavailable or a verified limitation blocks a required capability, and record why. Inspect key frames and the full video; verify dimensions, duration, frame rate, audio, and continuity.
